rss.title: +10 kg vs ×1.5 Every 2 Seconds / Physics Simulation #satisfyingsounds #asmr #blenderanimation
rss.desc:
A follower asked: two 1 kg steel balls, one gains 10 kg every 2 seconds, the other gets 1.5 times heavier every 2 seconds – which one breaks the 1 t glass? Two identical glass domes, two identical towers of 960 loose cubes, the same throw. The +10 kg ball leads for 22 seconds. Then the ×1.5 ball overtakes, hits the glass with 985 kg – it holds – and breaks it two seconds later with 1,478 kg. The +10 kg ball would need 200 seconds. The balls' rules are made up; everything the cubes do is real rigid-body physics. Simulated with Bullet, rendered in Blender. Which one did you bet on?

#satisfyingvideo #satisfying #blender #blender3d #physics

rss.title: Faster vs More vs Bigger / Physics Simulation #satisfyingsounds #asmr #blenderanimation
rss.desc:
Three identical glass domes, three towers of 960 loose cubes, the same steel ball, the same throw. Left: every bounce makes the ball 1.215 times faster. Back: every bounce adds one more ball. Right: every bounce makes the ball 1.3 times bigger. Whoever breaks the glass first wins. For 11 seconds all three look harmless – then the fast ball goes from 167 to 6,734 km/h in a third of a second, the back dome fills up with 1,482 balls and the right ball grows to 5.4 m. The balls' rules are made up; everything the cubes do is real rigid-body physics. Simulated with Bullet, rendered in Blender. Which one did you bet on?

rss.title: +10 vs ×1.5 Every Second / Physics Simulation #satisfyingsounds #asmr #blenderanimation
rss.desc:
A blue and a red ball in a glass dome with a tower of 960 white cubes. Every second blue gets 10 more balls and red is multiplied by 1.5. A cube takes the colour of the last ball that touched it. Blue is far ahead for 14 seconds – then red takes over. After 20 seconds 4,486 balls no longer fit and the dome bursts. The cubes are counted into towers: the colour with more cubes wins. The balls' rule is made up; everything the cubes do is real rigid-body physics. Simulated with Bullet, rendered in Blender. When did you see it coming?
